Bearing Inspection

Inspect machine bearings for wear, damage, unusual noise, and abnormal movement.

Damaged bearings should be replaced according to the approved maintenance procedure.

Record bearing inspection results after maintenance.

Drive Belt Maintenance

Inspect drive belts for wear, cracks, looseness, or visible damage.

A damaged or worn belt should be replaced according to the approved maintenance procedure.

Verify proper belt tension before restarting the equipment.

Electrical Safety Procedure

Before inspecting or repairing equipment, disconnect the main power supply.

Verify that the equipment is completely isolated before beginning maintenance.

Technicians must follow the approved electrical safety procedure.

ac83ba57a1a7894b3b7f6388431a8f2ec2ddc509.text:
Equipment Restart Procedure

After maintenance is completed, verify that all tools have been removed from the machine.

Confirm that safety checks have been completed before restarting the equipment.

Only restart the machine when the equipment is safe to operate.

Inspect the lubrication system regularly.

Check lubricant levels and inspect the equipment for leaks.

Use the approved lubricant specified for the equipment.

Abnormal vibration can indicate a problem with machine components. Inspect the machine for unusual movement, noise, loose components, and visible damage.

If abnormal vibration is detected, stop the machine and begin the approved inspection procedure.

Vibration Inspection Procedure

If unusual vibration is detected during machine operation, stop the equipment immediately.

Inspect the machine for loose components, damaged bearings, worn belts, and other mechanical problems.

Do not restart the equipment until the inspection has been completed and the machine is considered safe.
